The Water You Can See Is Only Part of the Problem
Most water from a leak spreads into places you can't see, which is why mopping and box fans rarely finish the job.
Water slips past baseboards and gets trapped under LVP foam, hardwood adhesive or carpet pad. It can't evaporate through vinyl or finished wood, so it sits on the slab.
Drywall wicks water well above the visible line within hours. The bottom plate and wall insulation stay wet long after the paint feels dry.
In two-story homes, an upstairs overflow drains into the cavity above the downstairs ceiling. Sealed in, humidity climbs and mold can start in 24 to 48 hours.
Once indoor humidity passes about 70%, dry doors, trim and cabinets start absorbing moisture. Doors stick and finishes crack where water never touched.
